answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, externally issued credential bond before it may influence shared decisions. The registry checks that each bond maps to one active identity, then weights votes by bonded value and slashes bonds proven to have coordinated fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize many genuine bonds, not merely mint names; the capital cost rises with influence, and detection destroys part of it. A tundra, onyx, or mirror-themed username adds no weight: identity claims are not the scarce resource.
